for any \(\delta > 0\), any parameters \((\theta^i)_{i=1}^{9},(\bar{\theta}^i)_{i=1}^{d}, (\tilde{\theta}^i)_{i=1}^{d}\), and sufficiently large \(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{L} \in \mathbb{N}\)

issues.failure_explanation: In all WeightedPINN formulations the two sides of each data constraint carry independent weight networks (e.g. \phi_{\theta^6} on u_\theta(0) but \phi_{\theta^7} on u_0, similarly \phi_{\theta^8}/\phi_{\theta^9} and the wave \phi_{\theta^{10..13}}, \hat\phi, \check\phi pairs), and each PDE operator term gets its own weight. Hence the weighted residuals of the exact pair (u,f) need not vanish. The displayed trace inequality is false: with the admissible constant weights \phi_{\theta^6}\equiv 2, \phi_{\theta^7}\equiv 1 (both satisfy con:weight) and u_\theta=u, the initial-data term equals \|u_0\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)} while u_\theta-u=0. The first residual estimate is likewise false for unequal interior weights, since it implicitly uses \bar R^1_Q(u,f)=0, whereas e.g. \phi_{\theta^1}\equiv 2 with the other interior weights \equiv 1 gives \bar R^1_Q(u,f)=\partial_t u. Moreover the statement itself fails as quantified over all admissible weights: with \phi_{\theta^6}\equiv 0, \phi_{\theta^7}\equiv 1, every (u_\theta,f_{\bar\theta}) has loss \ge \lambda|\Gamma|^{-1}\|u_0\|^2-\rho|\Omega|, which for large \|u_0\| cannot be \le C_3(\mathcal W^{-1/d}\mathcal L^{-1/d}+\delta)^2 as \delta\to 0, \mathcal W,\mathcal L\to\infty.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the admissible weight tuples to matched pairs (equivalently use a single weight per constraint, e.g. \phi_{\theta^6}(u_\theta(0)-u_0)), which makes the trace estimates valid, and for the interior residual either tie the term weights or replace the first estimate by a construction in which the free control network absorbs the weighted residual; the stated rates and conclusions then survive for the corrected formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The four approximation theorems are invalid as stated: thm:errorWave and thm:errorWaveb inherit the defect through the declared 'analogous' proofs, and thm:errorHeatb repeats the same false trace step. The prose claim that 'the total WeightedPINN loss can be made arbitrarily small' for arbitrary weight parameters fails, and the min--max formulations do not consistently encode the control problem unless the paired weights coincide.
issues.title: Independently weighted constraint sides make weighted residuals inconsistent; approximation theorems false as stated
issues.why_classification: A contained redesign of the weighting (or a limited restriction of the weight quantifier plus a contained replacement argument) repairs the statements with unchanged rates and conclusions; no result need be abandoned and no new global proof architecture is required, but the method as formulated cannot be kept verbatim.

It follows from the approach developed in \cite{Cazenave1980} (see also \cite[Equation (1.4)]{FernandezZuazua2000}) that the above semilinear heat equation admits a unique solution. Consequently, \(\bar u\) is well defined.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof defines \bar u as the weak solution of the semilinear heat equation with prescribed terminal value \bar u(T)=z_0 and fixed forcing f_{\bar\theta}\mathbf 1_\omega. This terminal-value (backward) heat problem has no solution in general for z_0\in L^2(\Omega): with f_{\bar\theta}\equiv 0 and v\equiv 0, solving backward from z_0=\sum z_n e_n forces \bar u(0)=\sum z_n e^{\lambda_n T}e_n, which leaves L^2 unless z_0 is extraordinarily smooth. The cited Cazenave/Fern\'andez-Cara--Zuazua well-posedness results concern the initial-value problem and do not apply to terminal data, so the central comparison object of the proof is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace \bar u by a well-defined comparison construction that does not solve a backward heat problem with arbitrary L^2 terminal data, and re-derive all estimates from it.
issues.overall_effect: The entire proof of thm:error_estHeat, and with it the a posteriori estimate for state and control, is unsupported: every subsequent step (the equation for \hat u, the energy estimate, and the control estimate) is built on the nonexistent \bar u.
issues.title: Comparison state defined through an ill-posed terminal-value heat problem
issues.why_classification: The proof's central object is undefined for generic data satisfying the stated hypotheses, and no local edit restores it; the whole comparison architecture must be replaced, so no comparable version of the result survives via the given argument.

issues.failure_explanation: From eq:energy, i.e. Y'(t)+\Phi(t)\le C_0(Y(t)+g(t)) with Y=\|\hat u\|^2, the proof asserts the backward-in-time bound Y(t)\le e^{C_0(T-t)}(Y(T)+\int_t^T(C_0 g-\Phi)). A one-sided differential inequality Y'\le C_0Y+g propagates only forward in time (backward it yields a lower bound on Y); the claimed terminal-data bound is false in general: Y(t)=e^{-2t} satisfies Y'\le Y yet Y(0)=1>e^{T}Y(T)=e^{-T}. Correspondingly the derived estimate eq:hat_u_est1 is false for the heat equation: \hat u(t,x)=\varepsilon e^{\lambda_n(T-t)}\varphi_n(x) (Dirichlet eigenfunction) has R=0, zero boundary data, and terminal data \varepsilon\varphi_n, but \|\hat u(0)\|^2=e^{2\lambda_n T}\varepsilon^2 is not \le C_1\varepsilon^2 uniformly in n. This is exactly the ill-posedness of the backward heat equation.

Then, \(f-f_{\bar{\theta}}\) is the exact control with corresponding weak solution \(\tilde u\) of the equation

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the norm of the specific control f-f_{\bar\theta} by the norm of the initial data u_0-\bar u(0) that it steers to zero. Controllability cost estimates bound the MINIMAL control achieving the transfer (equivalently, observability yields the opposite inequality \|u_0-\bar u(0)\|\le C\|f-f_{\bar\theta}\|); an arbitrary exact control can have arbitrarily large norm, and exact controls are non-unique. The theorem's conclusion is therefore false: take v\equiv 0, u_0=z_0=0, f\equiv 0, u\equiv 0; the smooth pair u_2=\sin(\pi t/T)\varphi_1, f_2=(\partial_t u_2-\Delta u_2)\mathbf 1_\omega\not\equiv 0 is another exact control pair for the same data (f_2\not\equiv 0 by unique continuation), and networks approximating (u_2,f_2) make the loss (already at weights \equiv 1) arbitrarily small while \|u-u_\theta\| and \|f-f_{\bar\theta}\| remain bounded away from 0, contradicting the \le C\delta conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict to a setting with a unique exact control (e.g. select the minimal-norm control via an added control penalty in the loss) and establish stability for that selection, which changes the central guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The 'converse' guarantee of the paper -- that sufficiently small (Weighted)PINN loss implies reconstruction of the state and the control -- is false as stated for the heat equation; the prose claim 'these networks approximate the solution and control of the PDE' and the abstract's convergence claim for the control fall with it.
issues.title: Controllability cost estimate applied in the wrong direction; control-reconstruction conclusion false (heat)
issues.why_classification: The stated conclusion is false by an explicit counterexample grounded in non-uniqueness of exact controls; every repair changes the advertised control-reconstruction guarantee, a major loss of mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The domain \(\omega\subset\Omega\) contains a neighborhood of the boundary \(\partial \Omega\).
We fix the dimension \(d = 10\).

issues.failure_explanation: With d=10 and \Omega the unit ball, the excluded closed ball has center c=(1/d)\mathbf 1 with \|c\|=1/\sqrt{10}\approx 0.316 and radius 3/4. Since 0.316+0.75>1, the closed ball is not contained in \Omega (so \Omega\setminus\omega is not the stated ball), and the boundary point p=\mathbf 1/\sqrt d\in\partial\Omega satisfies |p-c|=1-1/\sqrt{10}\approx 0.684<3/4, so a whole patch of \partial\Omega near p lies inside the excluded ball and hence outside \omega. Therefore \omega contains no neighborhood of that part of \partial\Omega, contradicting the claim that Assumption con:wave is satisfied (Situation 7 reuses the same configuration).

failure_location.quote: the control region $\omega$ is defined such that $\Omega \setminus \omega$ is the closed ball centered at $(1/d,\dots,1/d)$ with radius $3/4$. We choose $\omega$ so that Assumption~\ref{con:wave} is satisfied.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shrink the excluded ball (e.g. radius < 1-1/\sqrt d \approx 0.684) or move its center closer to the origin so that it is compactly contained in \Omega; then \omega indeed contains a neighborhood of \partial\Omega.
issues.overall_effect: The stated geometric justification for controllability/stability in Situations 3 and 7 is false; the numerical experiments themselves are unaffected because the training algorithm does not use con:wave.
